text.title: Continuous Discovery Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on weekly customer access, the existence of a single team-controllable product outcome, and who actually conducts the touchpoints — to a full opportunity-solution-tree cadence, a halt to restate the outcome, or a skip when the weekly floor cannot be met.

decision-tree.root-question: Can the team reach at least one customer or well-qualified prospect every week without a gatekeeper scheduling it for them?

branch.when: no reachable audience yet, procurement-gated buyers, or a user population with no consent path — weeks would pass with zero touches

conclusion.verdict: skip; emit a structured skip naming the access blocker and route to a one-off research burst or an audience-building step first

branch.when: a recurring weekly conversation slot is genuinely bookable with real customers or prospects
branch.question: Is the target for the cycle a customer behaviour the team can move, or a business number (ARR, revenue, retention target) handed down from above?

branch.when: the only stated target is a business number or a feature ship date, with no behaviour behind it

conclusion.verdict: halt; translate the business target into exactly one product outcome — a customer behaviour — before any opportunity tree is drawn

branch.when: one product outcome expressed as customer behaviour is agreed for the cycle
branch.question: Who conducts the weekly touchpoints — a member of the product trio, or sales, support tickets and an external agency relaying findings?

branch.when: research is relayed second-hand by sales, support or an agency and the trio never speaks to a customer

conclusion.verdict: do not open the tree; the product trio must conduct the touchpoints itself — relayed findings do not satisfy the weekly floor

branch.when: product, design or engineering run the conversations themselves

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; log every touch, phrase opportunities as needs traced to past-tense stories, compare 3 solutions before any test, and pre-write each kill threshold
